_comment: PROPOSAL rev B: 3D general arrangement, fitted to the sim's room graph (ship.json). Frame: metres; x fore(+)/aft(-), y starboard(+)/port(-), z up(+); origin amidships on the main-deck floor. Rooms are boxes. A room's local coordinate u (left to right in its side-on camera) comes from axis + origin: '+x' u = x - origin, '-x' u = origin - x, '+y' u = y - origin, '-y' u = origin - y. 'view' is the wall the room camera faces. Rooms marked new are suggestions the sim does not have yet. Hatches give 3D door points (or a path for ladders and crawls). Shafts are ladder wells, lifts and vertical vents; ducts are the crawlable vent network. tools/ship3d.mjs checks all of it.
name: Long-range survey ship
summary: A 138 m, single-occupant survey ship in the Krait mould: a flat, wide top deck over a belly that hangs below it, two flat tines running forward from the deck to blunt tips, and two big thrusters housed in the rear corners of the hull. A deckhouse amidships-aft holds the living deck, and the bridge sits in a raised tower on top of it, looking forward over the whole length of the ship.

rooms.info: Top of the tower, under a raked canopy. Helm, nav, scanner and terminal face forward over the whole length of the hull and the forked bow. The ladder from the living deck comes up through a floor hatch in the middle of the room.
Spine of the living deck. The bridge ladder rises from its aft end, the trunk ladder drops to the main deck at its forward end.
Along the starboard wall of the deckhouse, behind its longest window, looking out across the dorsal hull and the radiators. Couch, easel, speaker and room to exercise.
Starboard, forward of the lounge. Pantry, stove, counter and a table by a starboard porthole.
Port side. Bunk, basin, desk, locker and the torpor pod, with a porthole out to port.
Service spine of the main deck, directly under the living-deck spine. Six compartments open off it; engineering is through the bulkhead at its aft end.

Starboard, running outboard from the corridor all the way to the hull: ten grow trays, the algae tank, the seed bank and two pumps, with a long window in the sloping flank at the far end. The plumbing crawlway leaves from its aft side.
rooms.resize: lengthened from 12 m to 19.9 m so the bay reaches the hull's starboard flank and gets daylight through its own window strip

rooms.info: Starboard, back to back with hydroponics so the water mains are short. Recycler, oxygen generator, CO₂ scrubber and dehumidifier.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Starboard, aft. Bench, fabricator and lathe, with a door straight through to engineering.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Port side. Shelves and crates of spares, feedstock and food.

virtualWindow.note: a wall screen showing that exterior camera, in place of a real window

rooms.info: Against the port hull now, at the end of its own passage: inner door from the passage, suit rack, and an outer door straight to space that opens onto an external lift down to the ground.

Full-width compartment at the aft end of the pressurized decks. Its camera looks aft at the shadow-shield bulkhead: scoop manifold to starboard, the reactor face on the centreline, drive coupling to port.

rooms.name: Gym
rooms.info: Treadmill, rower and a resistance rig at the forward end of the deckhouse. Long voyages need more than the lounge's exercise corner.

rooms.name: Forward lookout
rooms.info: Short passage ending at the deckhouse's glazed front: a standing view over the forward hull. The freight lift opens off it.

rooms.name: Medbay
rooms.info: Diagnostic bed, autodoc arm, pharmacy locker. Near the bridge ladder and the lift, so an injured traveler is never far from it.

rooms.name: Washroom
rooms.info: Shower, toilet and laundry. Washing happens at the quarters basin today.

rooms.name: Forward service passage
rooms.info: Continues the service spine forward to the lab, the data core, the stores and the refinery. The forward ladder well drops to the lower deck from here.

rooms.name: Survey laboratory
rooms.info: Glovebox, spectrometer, core racks and a microscope bench. Samples come up from the hold on the freight lift and get analysed here.

rooms.name: Data & navigation core
rooms.info: The ship computer's racks, the star catalogue and the survey archive, in a cool, quiet room.

rooms.name: Spares & feedstock store
rooms.info: Bulk spares, fabricator feedstock and long-term food, next to the freight lift.

rooms.name: Refinery
rooms.info: Crushes and sorts ore and ice from the bunkers below into fabricator feedstock and water.

rooms.name: Lower passage
rooms.info: Runs the length of the lower deck between the hold and the rover bay. Both ladder wells and the freight lift come down to it.

rooms.name: Cargo & sample hold
rooms.info: Racks of sealed sample cases, ore drums and bulk stores. Samples are tracked as cargo today but have no room.

rooms.name: Rover bay
rooms.info: Unpressurized garage for the surface rover. The traveler reaches it suited, down the ladder from the airlock's outer hatch. The bay floor is a platform that lowers the rover to the ground and raises it again.

rooms.name: Skiff bay
rooms.info: Hangar for the survey skiff, at the forward end of the lower passage. The bay depressurizes and its belly doors open to drop the skiff clear of the hull.

rooms.name: Starboard gallery
rooms.info: A long observation walkway against the starboard side of the hull, with windows in the sloping wall looking out and down. Reached by the cross passage.

rooms.name: Port gallery
rooms.info: A long observation walkway against the port side of the hull, looking out and down.

rooms.name: Cross passage
rooms.info: Runs across the ship from the end of the forward service passage to both galleries.

rooms.name: Airlock passage
rooms.info: Runs from the service spine out to the airlock against the port hull. The sim's corridor-to-airlock crossing would grow from 7 s to about 20 s.

rooms.name: Rover suit lock
rooms.info: Small lock between the lower passage and the unpressurized rover bay: suit up here, cycle, walk out to the rover.

hatches.note: ladder well up through the deckhouse roof into the bridge
the trunk ladder between the two spines
a run of the under-floor crawl duct, beside the water mains

shafts.name: Trunk ladder well
shafts.info: The main ladder well, through all three hull decks at the forward end of the two spines. The sim's spine hatch is its upper half.

shafts.name: Bridge ladder well
shafts.info: From the aft end of the living spine up through the deckhouse roof into the bridge.

shafts.name: Forward ladder well
shafts.info: Second way between the main and lower decks, so the hold and rover bay are never one hatch from being cut off.

shafts.name: Freight lift
shafts.info: 4.2 m platform rated for six tonnes, serving the lower, main and living decks: sample cases from the hold, reactor spares, crates for the galley, a stretcher to the medbay.

shafts.name: Rover bay platform
shafts.info: The bay floor drops through the belly on four screw jacks, lowering the rover to the ground when landed and raising it back in.

shafts.name: Aft vent shaft
shafts.info: Vertical vent with rungs, behind engineering: joins the main-deck overhead duct to the deckhouse roof duct.

shafts.name: Forward vent shaft
shafts.info: Vertical vent with rungs at the forward end of the service spine: joins the overhead duct to the under-floor crawl.

shafts.name: Skiff bay doors
shafts.info: Clamshell doors in the belly. The skiff drops out on its own lift fans and comes back up the same way.

shafts.name: External EVA lift
shafts.info: A cage on the outside of the hull by the airlock's outer door. It lowers a suited traveler to the ground and brings them back up.

ducts.name: Main-deck overhead duct
ducts.info: Air returns and cable trays in the 1.4 m void above the main deck. 0.9 m square and crawlable, with a ceiling grille into every compartment it passes.

ducts.name: Under-floor crawl
ducts.info: Crawlspace beneath the main-deck plates, beside the water mains and power trunks. The plumbing crawl between life support and hydroponics is one run of it.

ducts.name: Deckhouse roof duct
ducts.info: Air handling above the living deck, under the deckhouse roof. Grilles into every cabin; the aft vent shaft drops from its end.

modules.name: Sensor array (port prong)
modules.info: Long-baseline survey sensors. The two prongs together give a 23 m baseline.

modules.name: Sensor array (starboard prong)
modules.info: Long-baseline survey sensors.

modules.name: Scoop processing plant
modules.info: Separates and chills scooped hydrogen before it goes aft to the tanks.

modules.name: Water & consumables tanks
modules.info: Potable water, grey water and bulk nutrient stock.

modules.name: Ore & ice bunkers
modules.info: Raw material waiting for the refinery above.

modules.name: Fuel tank (port)
modules.info: Liquid hydrogen, moved aft into the thruster housing. With its twin, about 30 t usable.

modules.name: Fuel tank (starboard)
modules.info: Liquid hydrogen, moved aft into the thruster housing. With its twin, about 30 t usable.

modules.name: Shadow-shield bulkhead
modules.info: Radiation shield between the reactor and the pressurized decks. Engineering's camera looks straight at it.

modules.name: Fusion reactor
modules.info: Main power plant, behind the shield on the centreline.

modules.name: Frame-shift drive
modules.info: Hyperspace coil assembly. Wears with each jump.

modules.name: Main drive block
modules.info: Thruster feed, gimbals and the supercruise field generator.

modules.name: Radiator panels (port)
modules.info: Radiator panels laid flush on top of the port thruster housing. They glow on the stern camera when the ship runs hot.

modules.name: Air handlers & water tanks
modules.info: Deckhouse air handling and a day tank of water, aft of the living spaces.

modules.name: Sensor & comms racks
modules.info: Electronics behind the bridge, under the mast.

modules.name: Sensor mast & nav beacon
modules.info: Carries the dorsal camera and a blinking beacon.

modules.name: Surface rover
modules.info: Six-wheeled, two-seat pressurized rover for long ground traverses and heavy sampling: rock cores, drums of ice, crates of specimens. Parked on the bay platform.

modules.name: Fuel scoop intake (ventral)
modules.info: Under the forward belly. The ship skims a star belly-first, so the intake faces the plasma while the windows look away.

modules.name: Survey skiff
modules.info: A small two-seat VTOL flyer for aerial survey: it drops out of the belly bay, maps terrain from the air, grabs samples from places the rover can't reach (cliff faces, ice shelves, the far side of a ravine) and flies them home.

modules.info: One of twelve nozzles in a 4 × 3 bank, set back inside the housing's rim. Together they are the main thruster on this side.

modules.name: Port inboard engine
modules.info: Trim and backup engine, recessed in the inboard housing between the two main banks.

exterior.name: Dorsal camera
exterior.info: On the mast, looking forward over the bridge canopy along the whole dorsal hull to the bow prongs. The old hull camera, moved.

exterior.name: Bow camera
exterior.info: On the blunt tip of the starboard tine, looking back along the flank at the deckhouse and tower. The hero shot for arrivals and star skimming.

exterior.name: Scoop camera
exterior.info: Under the bow just ahead of the ventral intake, looking forward: the star filling the frame while the ship skims it belly-first.

exterior.name: Stern camera
exterior.info: On the aft face of the deckhouse, looking down over the radiators to the four engines. Engine glow, the radiators running hot, the wake of a jump.

exterior.name: Port flank camera
exterior.info: On the port deck edge aft, looking forward along the port side.

exterior.name: Starboard flank camera
exterior.info: On the starboard deck edge aft, looking forward along the starboard side.

exterior.name: Ventral camera
exterior.info: Under the bow, looking aft along the belly: landing gear, the rover platform going down, the ground coming up on landing.

exterior.name: Rover bay camera
exterior.info: Inside the unpressurized bay, looking across the platform and the rover.

exterior.name: Rover camera
exterior.info: On the rover's mast. Out on the surface it follows the drive; in the bay it looks at the bay door.

exterior.name: Skiff camera
exterior.info: On the skiff's nose. In flight it looks down at the ground it is mapping; in the bay it watches the doors.

windowNotes.hydro: deep in the hull: the window strip becomes a grow-light panel
windowNotes.airlock: the outer door is a floor hatch to the rover bay

windows.name: Bow window
windows.info: Glazing across the face between the tines, looking straight ahead along the line of flight.

windows.name: Port deck windows
windows.info: A long strip set flush into the top deck near its port edge.

windows.name: Starboard deck windows
windows.info: A long strip set flush into the top deck near its starboard edge.

windows.name: Port tine window
windows.info: Flush in the top of the port tine, looking up and forward.

windows.name: Starboard tine window
windows.info: Flush in the top of the starboard tine.

windows.name: Starboard gallery windows
windows.info: Glazing in the sloping underside of the starboard wing, along the gallery.

windows.name: Port gallery windows
windows.info: Glazing in the sloping underside of the port wing, along the gallery.

windows.name: Rover bay windows
windows.faces: out to port, below the wing
windows.info: Ports in the port wall of the belly, looking out from the rover bay.

windows.name: Hold windows
windows.faces: out to starboard, below the wing
windows.info: Ports in the starboard wall of the belly, beside the hold.

windows.name: Skiff bay windows (starboard)
windows.info: Ports in the belly wall of the skiff bay.

windows.name: Skiff bay windows (port)
windows.info: Ports in the belly wall of the skiff bay.

windows.name: Hydroponics window
windows.info: Daylight for the grow trays: a strip in the sloping starboard flank at the outboard end of the bay.

windows.name: Airlock outer door port
windows.info: The porthole in the airlock's outer door, set in the port flank.

windowShutters: Every window has an armoured shutter. Shutters close for supercruise, hyperspace, scooping and anywhere near a strong radiation source, and open when the ship is holding station somewhere safe.
